HomePage.heroText: We find where you overpay for electricity, heat and water, compare the options and prepare the project. We work with communities, businesses, homeowners’ associations and homeowners.
HomePage.whyTitle: Electricity is the easiest place to start
HomePage.whyText: It is easy to measure: there is a meter and there are bills. But if heating or water is the problem, we start there.

whyItems.title: The meter is already there
whyItems.text: Readings and bills show when and how much you use.

whyItems.title: We compare options
whyItems.text: We work out several solutions before any equipment is bought.

whyItems.title: We check the result
whyItems.text: We compare costs before and after the changes.

whyItems.title: Everything is connected
whyItems.text: Pumps and boilers run on electricity, so a change in one system affects the others.

HomePage.whyFooter: We suggest solar panels and batteries only when the numbers show they pay off for you.
HomePage.segmentsText: Everyone has their own tasks and budget, so each has its own section.

segments.title: Communities and utilities
segments.text: Networks, boiler houses, water supply and sewerage, schools and hospitals.

segments.title: Business and industry
segments.text: Reliable power, heat and water for production without unnecessary costs.

segments.title: Homeowner associations
segments.text: Shared building systems, metering and a repair plan.

segments.title: Developers and investors

segments.title: Private owners
segments.text: Electricity, heating and water in your home.

HomePage.competenciesText: Before we start, we agree on what we do, who is responsible for what and how we will check the result.

competencies.title: Survey
competencies.text: We look at how electricity, heat and water work, where the losses are and what is missing.

dialog.why: To choose a solution for your site, not for equipment someone wants to sell.
dialog.data: Drawings, meter readings, bills, operating schedule, a list of problems. If something is missing, we tell you what to collect.
dialog.result: A description of how the systems work now, a list of problems and a plan of next steps.
dialog.limits: A survey does not replace mandatory inspections or design documents.
dialog.next: Describe the site and the problem, and we will agree on the first step.

competencies.title: Analysis
competencies.text: We compare options by cost, reliability and benefit.

dialog.why: To understand what to do first.
dialog.data: Survey results, metering data, constraints and budget.
dialog.result: A comparison of options and the order of measures.
dialog.limits: A preliminary calculation is an estimate, not a guarantee of savings or payback.
dialog.next: Tell us what matters most to you, and we will compare the options.

competencies.title: Solution
competencies.text: We prepare a concept, a technical specification and calculations for an investor or a programme.

dialog.why: To have a clear document for a decision, a tender or fundraising.
dialog.data: The chosen option, site data, budget and who makes the decision.
dialog.result: A concept, pre-feasibility study or technical specification — we agree on which one in advance.
dialog.limits: These documents do not replace design work or permits.
dialog.next: Tell us what decision needs to be made, and we will prepare the documents.

competencies.title: Support
competencies.text: We help with procurement and check the result after the works.

dialog.why: To get what you ordered and see the effect in numbers.
dialog.data: Specification, contractor offers, work schedule, metering before and after.
dialog.result: A comparison of offers, a check of the works and a report on the result.
dialog.limits: Our role and the contractors' responsibilities are set out in the contract.
dialog.next: Tell us what stage the project is at, and we will suggest how we can help.

SystemDiagram.ariaLabel: Diagram of the site's energy system elements
SystemDiagram.footer: This diagram is illustrative. The actual system composition for a specific site is determined after a survey.

nodes.label: Solar
details: Generates energy during the day, depending on sunlight
Capacity is sized to the consumption profile, not the roof area
Surplus is either stored or fed back into the grid

nodes.label: Storage
details: Stores surplus generation and off-peak tariff energy
Lifespan is measured in cycles, not years

nodes.label: Load
details: The consumption profile determines what's even worth installing
Without measuring the profile, the payback calculation is unreliable

nodes.label: Control
details: Decides when to charge, when to discharge, when to draw from the grid
Accounts for the tariff, generation forecast, and connection limits
Without this layer, equipment operates blindly

nodes.label: Metering
details: Records what's consumed and what's fed back into the grid
The basis for settlements with the supplier
Metering data is the starting point of any energy audit

nodes.label: Grid
details: The distribution system operator, the connection point
Connection capacity limits everything that can be installed
Grid feed-in terms are set by contract

AboutPage.title: CEE: site engineering as a connected system
AboutPage.intro: The Ladyzhyn Energy Efficiency Centre works on electricity, heat, water supply and wastewater for communities, businesses, homeowner associations and private owners. We gather evidence, prepare options and support agreed stages with defined client and contractor responsibilities.

principles.title: Evidence first
principles.text: We distinguish measurements from assumptions and identify missing information.

principles.title: Connected systems
principles.text: Electrical decisions are assessed alongside heat, water and wastewater needs.

principles.title: Needs-based priorities
principles.text: Safety, reliability, asset condition and cost determine the sequence. Electricity does not always come first.

principles.title: Outcome verification
principles.text: We agree the baseline and indicators before implementation, then check actual changes.

CitizensPage.heroTitle: Electricity, heat and water in your home
CitizensPage.heroText: We help you understand where your money for power, heating and water goes and what is worth changing. Solar panels and a battery are just one of the options.
CitizensPage.whyTitle: Heat, light and control over costs
CitizensPage.whyText: We choose solutions for your home. We do not promise savings without a calculation.

whyItems.title: What your family needs

whyItems.title: Bills and metering

whyItems.title: Step by step

BusinessPage.heroTitle: Electricity, heat and water for business
BusinessPage.heroText: Outages and unnecessary resource costs hit your profit. We find where money is lost and what to do first. We suggest a solar plant or a battery only if the numbers show a benefit.
BusinessPage.whyText: We compare options by their effect on production and their full cost.

whyItems.title: What you spend

whyItems.title: No downtime

whyItems.title: A sound investment
whyItems.text: We calculate the payback of several options. It is a forecast, not a guarantee.

ServicesPage.heroText: Electricity, heat, water and wastewater: from surveys and concepts to investment preparation, procurement support and monitoring. We agree the scope, inputs and expected outputs for each stage.
ServicesPage.windowText: CEE helps connect technical, organisational and financial tasks. Team roles, scope and specialist involvement are defined to suit each project.

window.title: A clear task
window.text: Clarify the need and agree measurable stage outputs.

window.title: Transparent roles
window.text: Define the responsibilities of CEE, the client and specialist contractors.

window.title: Criteria-based verification
window.text: Compare outputs with the agreed specification and record constraints and deviations.

ServicesPage.formatsText: Commission an individual stage or coordinated support across several stages. Responsibilities and required approvals are agreed before work starts.

formats.title: A defined task
formats.text: A survey, analysis, concept or specification with agreed outputs.

formats.title: Project preparation
formats.text: A sequence from evidence and options to an investment package and procurement requirements.

formats.title: Support and monitoring
formats.text: Agreed advice, checkpoints and performance analysis during and after implementation.

ServicesPage.productsText: These services apply across all four fields. Detailed outputs depend on site condition, data quality and the agreed task.
ServicesPage.priceNote: Cost and timelines are set by scope after an initial conversation. There is no standard price list: scope depends on the state of the site, the data available and how deep we go.

products.name: Survey
products.task: Establish system condition and gaps in the available evidence.

products.name: Concept / pre-feasibility
products.task: Compare technical options and preliminary economics.

products.name: Technical specification
products.task: Define requirements for the next stage and acceptance criteria.

products.name: Investment preparation
products.task: Prepare material for a client, investor or funding-programme decision.

products.name: Procurement support
products.task: Help compare offers against agreed technical requirements.

products.name: Monitoring and verification
products.task: Assess actual system operation after implementation.

ServicesPage.digitalText: A project doesn't end when the equipment is switched on. For the result to be visible every day rather than once a year in a report, the site needs metering that collects data and a system that shows it and lets you act. If there isn't one, we set it up. If there is one but it doesn't work, we rebuild it.

digital.title: Modern metering systems
digital.text: Setting up or upgrading metering: devices, data collection, hourly consumption and generation profile. Without it, any effect is a guess, not a fact.

digital.title: Online tracking and control
digital.text: Live data from the site: consumption, generation, battery state, deviations from normal. Alerts when something goes wrong — before it shows up on the bill.

digital.title: Analytics for management
digital.text: Dashboards and reports that show exactly where the losses are, how the equipment performs and whether the result matches the calculation. For a director, a board or a donor — in plain form.

digital.title: Applications built for the project
digital.text: Software tools developed and adapted to a specific site, client and their processes. Not a generic panel like everyone else's, but something your people will actually use.

digital.title: Energy management system implementation
digital.text: Energy management as an ongoing process, not a one-off audit: policy, owners, indicators, regular review. Oriented on ISO 50001 logic, scaled to the size of the site.

ServicesPage.digitalFooter: The digital circuit is what makes the promise "we close with a result" verifiable. It is from its data that we confirm the effect after implementation.

aiModels.fallbackNote: Currently one OpenRouter call is allowed per request. Active approved models are ordered by priority, then ID for ties. A failure uses labeled local reference, not another LLM. Independent backup and five-level routing are not activated. The global allowance is 20 reserved attempts per 24 hours, not 20 guaranteed answers.
aiModels.configuredNotVerified: Configuration allowed and credential variable present; current operation and balance not verified
aiModels.providerNotApproved: This row or credential reference is not allowed for the primary OpenRouter model; independent backup is configured separately.
aiModels.operationFailed: Saving could not be confirmed. The form is preserved. Before creating again, refresh the list and check whether the record already exists.
aiModels.refreshFailed: The list could not be refreshed. If saving already completed, do not create it again: reload and verify the record first.
aiModels.backupEnabled: Independent backup is enabled by server configuration; this does not verify availability.
aiModels.backupPolicy: Backup policy order: OpenRouter → OpenAI (GPT-5.6 Luna) → Anthropic (Claude Haiku 5.5) → reference material. At most one attempt per provider, up to three overall; shared limits: 20 attempts per 24 hours, two unsettled attempts, and $2 of reserved backup usage over a rolling 24-hour window. Unknown cost stays reserved until reconciliation. Taxes, tariff changes and other applications are outside this limit. Backup requires current verified tariffs and its accounting table; reference material is not an LLM answer. Tariff validation expires at 2026-11-04 00:00 UTC; backup stops from that moment until review.
aiModels.backupTestWarning: Each click is one potentially billable call with fixed synthetic text, no customer data, and up to 64 output tokens. The shared 20-attempt and $2 backup limits apply. Another click is a separate attempt, not a replay of the same charge. Reconcile unknown outcomes before trying again; there are no automatic retries.
aiModels.backupTestSuccess: One synthetic response was received. This does not guarantee future availability or consultation quality.
aiModels.backupTestUnknown: The outcome is unknown or incomplete; billing is possible and the reservation is retained. Repeat checks on this page are blocked pending reconciliation.
aiModels.backupTestDenied: Admission denied: check authorization and available budget. Do not retry automatically.
aiModels.backupTestUnconfigured: Backup is disabled, configuration is missing, or tariff review is required.
aiModels.backupTestRefusal: The provider refused; no fallback or retry was made. Reconcile accounting before another attempt.
aiModels.backupTestAccounting: A response was received, but accounting settlement was not confirmed: the reservation remains held. Reconcile accounting first; further checks on this page are blocked.
aiModels.fallbackNoteWithBackups: For assistant chat, the first active approved OpenRouter model is selected by priority, then ID. On an eligible failure, the server may call OpenAI then Anthropic within the shared attempt and spending limits. Security refusals, access restrictions, key/organization spending restrictions and shared application limits are not bypassed. If no LLM answer is available, labeled reference material is shown. Document/digest generation remains a separate single invocation; connection-check buttons do not trigger a retry cascade either. Configuration does not verify provider availability.

PrivacyPage.label: Legal
PrivacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
PrivacyPage.intro: This policy explains what personal data the website of the Center for Energy Efficiency (Ladyzhyn) collects, why, for how long, and what rights you have. We collect only what is needed to reply to your request.

sections.title: Who processes the data
paragraphs: The controller of personal data is the Center for Energy Efficiency, Ladyzhyn, Vinnytsia region (the Center). Contact details are on the Contacts page.

sections.title: What data we collect
paragraphs: We process only the data you provide yourself on the site — via the request form, the assistant chat, or when registering a knowledge-base account:
items: your name or how to address you;
the type of your organisation or site (e.g. HOA, business, community);
the text of your request and, for chat requests, the conversation with the assistant;
the page the request was sent from and the interface language.

sections.title: Why we process it
paragraphs: The only purpose is to handle your request: contact you, clarify the situation and suggest where to start. The legal basis is your consent, given by ticking the box in the form or sending a contact in the chat.
We do not use your data for mailings without separate consent and do not pass it to third parties for advertising.

sections.title: The assistant on the site
paragraphs: The assistant replies based on the site's materials. If the Center has an external language model connected, the text of your message may be sent to that model's provider to generate a reply. Do not enter passport data, card numbers or other sensitive information in the chat — it is not needed to answer your question.

sections.title: Knowledge-base account
paragraphs: If you register, we store your email, name and organisation (optional), your password as an irreversible hash (bcrypt), your plan and the date of your last sign-in. To enforce plan limits we keep a count of consultant requests (date and request type) without storing the questions themselves beyond your session.
Sign-in uses a technical session cookie valid for up to 30 days or until you sign out. The account can be deleted on request together with all related data.

sections.title: Paid services and invoices
paragraphs: If you order a paid service or plan, we process the payer's name and details, the amount and the issue and payment dates in order to issue an invoice. This data is kept for as long as accounting law requires (at least three years after the reporting period). The site does not collect or store bank card details.

sections.title: Cookies and local storage
paragraphs: The site uses no advertising or tracking cookies. Only technical preferences are stored in your browser: the chosen theme, language and the current assistant conversation within a session, so it does not disappear between pages. This data does not leave your device.

sections.title: How long we keep it
paragraphs: Requests are kept as long as needed to handle them and communicate about your project, but no longer than three years from the last contact unless the law requires otherwise. Spam and erroneous requests are deleted.

sections.title: Who has access
paragraphs: Only authorised Center staff have access to requests. Technical services (hosting, database, mail server) may be used to store data and send emails; they process data on behalf of the Center and may not use it for their own purposes.

sections.title: Your rights
paragraphs: Under the Law of Ukraine "On Personal Data Protection" you have the right to:
items: know what data of yours we process and receive a copy;
To exercise any of these rights, write to us via the Contacts page form or the email listed there. We reply within 30 days.

sections.title: Changes to this policy
paragraphs: We may update this policy. The current version is always published on this page with the update date.

PrivacyPage.contact: Questions about personal data — via the Contacts page form, marked "personal data".

TermsPage.label: Legal
TermsPage.title: Terms of Use
TermsPage.intro: By using the website of the Center for Energy Efficiency you agree to these terms. They are simple: the information on the site is for reference, decisions about your site are made after a survey, and the assistant on the site is not a substitute for a specialist.

sections.title: What this site is
paragraphs: The site describes the Center's areas of work, the process and ways of working, and lets you leave a request. The site is not a public offer: the terms of specific cooperation are set by a separate agreement after discussing your task.

sections.title: Informational nature
paragraphs: All descriptions of services, stages and financing programmes are for reference. We verify programme data and indicate the verification date, but programme conditions change — check them directly with the programme administrator or bank before making financial decisions.
We do not publish figures we cannot back with a source, and we do not publish case studies without the client's written consent.

sections.title: The assistant on the site
paragraphs: The assistant replies based on the site's materials and does not invent figures, prices or timelines. Its replies are not a technical opinion, a commercial offer or legal advice. Decisions about your site are made after a survey and a conversation with a Center specialist.

sections.title: Requests
paragraphs: By sending a request you confirm that the contact details belong to you and agree that the Center will contact you to handle the request. Personal data processing is described in the Privacy Policy.

sections.title: Intellectual property
paragraphs: The texts, diagrams and design of the site belong to the Center. You may quote the site's materials with a reference to the source. Commercial use without the Center's consent is not permitted.

sections.title: Liability
paragraphs: The Center makes every effort to keep the information accurate and current, but does not guarantee uninterrupted operation of the site and is not liable for decisions made solely on the basis of information from the site without consulting a specialist.

sections.title: Changes
paragraphs: We may update these terms. The current version is always published on this page with the update date.

finance.text: Annuity loan or lease: monthly payment, total interest and whether the savings repay the financing within the term. Fits 'Energodim', bank loans for HOAs and business, ESCO.
finance.warn: Increase savings or term — not repaid by the end of the contract
finance.invalidAmount: Enter a financing amount greater than zero.

express.title: 60-second express estimate
express.text: Three short forms — a preliminary integration effect on typical coefficients. Full feasibility study after a consultation.

bess.title: Storage integration
bess.noConsumption: Nonzero consumption and peak power are required. No savings are projected for zero consumption.

express.note: Preliminary estimate. Exact figures after a site survey.

method.bessSizing: Illustrative capacity = peak power × 2 hours. This is not equipment selection: load profile, usable depth of discharge, efficiency and reserve are required. Use the detailed BESS calculation for economics.
method.solar: Illustrative assumptions: 7 m²/kW, 1150 kWh/kW per year, UAH 22000/kW. Self-consumption share is a user assumption. A forecast requires location, shading, orientation, losses and hourly demand.
method.illustration: Illustrative scenarios, not current tariffs or an offer. Enter your own prices and costs. Arbitrage uses an illustrative 24-hour profile and 92% round-trip efficiency; it is a heuristic, not a guaranteed optimum. Detailed BESS uses per-stage efficiency, 2% OPEX, 1.5% degradation from year two, 18% discount and a 15-year horizon. Annual figures assume 365 identical days; taxes, financing and replacements are excluded. Charging takes priority when selected charge/discharge hours overlap.
method.unbalanced: The daily cycle does not close: annual savings and investment metrics are undefined. Adjust charging/discharging hours or power.
method.infeasible: Load exceeds the connection power limit. Correct the inputs; annual economics are undefined.

Subscriptions.metaDescription: Subscriptions offered by the Centre for Energy Efficiency: retainer services (energy manager, monitoring, regulatory and procurement support) and knowledge-base access with the legislation consultant. What is included, how it is paid, how to start.
Subscriptions.label: Subscriptions
Subscriptions.title: Subscriptions: what exists and what is included
Subscriptions.intro: The Centre offers two kinds of subscriptions. Retainer services are regular work of our specialists with your site for a fixed monthly fee. The knowledge base is access to documents, digests and the legislation consultant on the website. Below is what each includes.
Subscriptions.servicesText: Instead of one-off requests, a Centre specialist keeps your site in view continuously. The price depends on the number of sites and depth — we quote it in reply to a request after a short call.

plans.name: Outsourced energy manager
plans.for: HOAs, municipal utilities, public institutions, SMEs
includes: Consumption control from meters and bills, comparison with the baseline
Monthly report: where costs grow and why
Prioritised savings plan with indicative effect
Answers for the board, manager and accountant
Support in dealings with the supplier and the DSO

plans.name: Monitoring and dashboards
plans.for: Sites with meters, AMR or own generation
includes: Automatic data collection (meters, AMR, SCADA, APIs)
Dashboards for the manager and energy manager (KPI/EnPI under ISO 50006)
Number of sites and update frequency are agreed for the specific service
Hosted on site or on your website

plans.name: Regulatory and procurement support
includes: Monthly review of NEURC, Parliament, Cabinet and ENTSO-E changes with a 'what it means for you' conclusion
Monitoring of support programmes, grants and tenders for your profile
Project compliance checks against the codes
Consultations on questions that arose during the month

plans.name: Full retainer
plans.for: Organisations with several sites or own generation
includes: Everything from the three plans above
Dedicated specialist and quarterly meeting with management
Priority for one-off work (feasibility studies, tenders, surveys)

Subscriptions.kbTitle: Access to documents, digests and the consultant
Subscriptions.kbText: This is a website subscription, not specialists’ work. Documents and digests are open to everyone. The consultant has a daily query allowance; registration raises it, and paid plans provide higher fair-use allowances. AI generation has a site-wide technical cap: 20 calls per rolling 24 hours and at most 2 requests with pending or uncertain outcomes. Uncertain requests may block new calls until manual reconciliation. A personal daily allowance does not guarantee generation capacity; a subscription does not bypass the shared cap.

kbPlans.name: Basic
kbPlans.text: Document catalogue, digests, search, consultant — {free} queries per day after registration ({guest} without it).

kbPlans.name: Premium
kbPlans.text: Up to 200 queries per day (fair use), query history, analytics and reviews for your site.

kbPlans.name: Enterprise
kbPlans.text: For organisations: up to 1000 queries per day (fair use), API access, several users.

steps.title: Request and call
steps.text: You describe the site and the task; we clarify the scope in 15–30 minutes.

steps.title: Proposal
steps.text: You receive a written proposal: what is included, monthly price, first step.

steps.title: Contract and invoice
steps.text: Contract, invoice, monthly act — everything for the accounting of an HOA, utility or company.

steps.title: Work and report
steps.text: First report within the first month. You can stop from the next month with prior notice.

faq.q: How does a subscription differ from a one-off service?
faq.a: A one-off service is a result with a clear boundary: a feasibility study, a certificate, a document package. A subscription is continuous attention to the site: control, reports, response to changes. Many start with a one-off survey and then move to a retainer.

faq.q: Can I combine a retainer with a knowledge-base subscription?
faq.a: Yes. Retainer services include Premium knowledge-base access for the client's responsible staff.
Meter data and documents are used only for work under the contract, kept on secured servers and not shared with third parties. Details in the Privacy Policy.
Currently payment is by invoice to a bank account. Card payment online will appear once a payment gateway is connected.

DirectionsPage.title: What we do
DirectionsPage.intro: Electricity, heat, water and sewerage. First we understand your needs and data, then we choose the equipment.
DirectionsPage.processTitle: From the task to the result
DirectionsPage.scopeNote: We define the scope of work and who is responsible for each site separately. A preliminary estimate does not replace a design.

items.title: Electricity supply
items.intro: Metering, reliable power, consumption peaks, backup and on-site generation.
tasks: When and how much you use, where the peaks and losses are.
What must always keep running and how to provide backup.
Comparing options: changing operating modes, a solar plant, a battery and more.
items.data: Meter readings, bills, network diagram, connection conditions, a list of important equipment.
items.result: What to do first, what it costs, what benefit it brings and how to check it.

items.title: Heat supply
items.intro: Boilers and boiler houses, heating networks, control and heat losses.
tasks: Heat and fuel metering, temperatures, losses.
How the boiler house, heat substation, pumps and networks work.
Comparing options: controls, modernisation, a heat pump.
items.data: Heat and fuel use, temperatures, operating schedule, building and equipment data.
items.result: Where heat is lost, a comparison of options and a modernisation plan.

items.title: Water supply
items.intro: Water supply and pressure, metering, losses and pumping costs.
tasks: How much water is supplied and how much arrives, where the leaks are.
How the pumps, backup and pressure work.
Whether water treatment is needed and which tests to do.
items.data: Supply and consumption volumes, pressure, network diagram, pump data, water tests.
items.result: A measurement plan and what to do to cut losses and supply water without interruptions.

items.title: Wastewater systems
items.intro: Sewer networks, pumping stations and wastewater treatment.
tasks: How much wastewater there is, what kind, and the state of the networks.
How the pumping stations work, backup and electricity use.
What treatment requires and which approvals are needed.
items.data: Wastewater volumes and tests, diagram of networks and facilities, incident logs, discharge requirements.
items.result: Which studies are needed, solution options, risks and the order of works.

process.title: Task
process.text: We find out what the problem is and what matters most to you.

process.title: Data
process.text: We collect readings, bills and information about the equipment.

process.title: Options
process.text: We compare them by safety, reliability, cost and benefit.

process.title: Solution
process.text: We prepare a concept, a specification and a work plan.

process.title: Check
process.text: We compare the result after the works with how things were before.

ClimateContent.name: Center for Energy Efficiency
ClimateContent.subtitle: Energy and climate resilience for the community

home.title: Energy and climate resilience for communities
home.body: We help communities and municipal utilities with electricity, heat, water and sewerage: we analyse consumption and the state of the networks, compare options and prepare technical requirements and concepts. The goal is more reliable services, lower losses and ready projects for modernisation.

community.title: From community needs to prepared projects
community.intro: We consider electricity, heat, water supply and wastewater services as interconnected systems. Solutions for individual facilities need to take account of community needs, infrastructure condition and the practical requirements of implementation.
community.helper: Describe the facility or system, the main problem and the baseline information available.
community.development: The energy hub development concept envisages consideration of climate risks, assessment of opportunities to reduce emissions, and preparation of pilot solutions together with the community and specialist partners.
community.financing: Project preparation and support in seeking funding do not guarantee a grant or investment.

items.title: An analytical foundation
items.text: Data on resource consumption, costs, technical condition and facility needs help identify problems and modernisation priorities.

items.title: Preparing solutions
items.text: Technical requirements, preliminary technical and economic assessments, and project concepts provide a basis for comparing options and planning next steps.

items.title: A project portfolio
items.text: For promising projects, we structure the need, expected outcome, preliminary cost, risks and readiness status. This provides a basis for discussions with partners and preparation for seeking funding.

items.title: Roles and responsibilities
items.text: CEE provides analytical and technical support within an agreed scope. The client sets priorities and allocates resources; specialist work is performed by appropriately qualified professionals. The scope of work and team are agreed for each project.

about.title: Energy hub concept for the Ladyzhyn community
about.body: The concept envisages a partnership platform bringing together the community, businesses, experts, educational and research institutions, and technology and financial partners around energy transition projects. The Center for Energy Efficiency is proposed as its organisational and expert core.
about.development: The energy hub development concept envisages consideration of climate risks, assessment of opportunities to reduce emissions, and preparation of pilot solutions together with the community and specialist partners.
about.clarification: This describes a development concept, not the establishment of a hub or approval of its status.
